# Visual reference screenshots

The English/Polish homepage files in this directory and `firefox/` are reviewed local Gatsby build captures from 2026-10-12, using Playwright 1.64.0 on Linux at 1440×900. The owner explicitly accepted the revised homepage composition and authorized updating these four references. The 3% tolerance remains unchanged. The current composition and acceptance are documented in [the proportions review](../../../docs/hero-proportions-review.md). Earlier production Firefox reference provenance remains in [the header visual review](../../../docs/header-visual-review.md).

The unnamed default Chromium run keeps the existing paths in this directory. `--browser firefox` uses `firefox/` through Playwright's native optional project-name template. Explicitly named browser runs require their own reviewed images; normal tests fail on missing references.

The homepage references originated as production captures on 2026-09-24 and were subsequently reviewed for intentional layout changes. Live archive/author/related/search captures were retired on 2026-10-12 because editorial changes altered their pixels without demonstrating layout regressions.

`components/` contains the controlled author/archive/related/search references reviewed by the owner on 2026-10-12: English/Polish at 390px and 1440px using Playwright 1.64.0 Chromium on Linux. They use the real presentation components, styles, shared fonts/theme and fixed synthetic text/cover from `tests/gallery/editorial.story.tsx`. Gatsby cover loading, localization and actual current content remain verified in the production-page/source suites. The test gallery is never published. The owner accepted the overall examples after being shown all four locale/viewport captures; screenshot tolerances remain unchanged.

`article-footer-production-legacy.png` and `article-reading-production-legacy.png` are diagnostic captures from the production article `/en/vertical-slices-and-dependencies/` on 2026-09-28. Production itself showed a different full article inside the author block because the old `/author/` query also matched a post slug containing `authorities`. These captures document the old state and are not active references. Current-source author checks and controlled `components/author-*.png` comparisons protect the corrected behavior.

Normal tests compare a locally served build (or `VISUAL_BASE_URL`) with these files and never contact production. To review the current screenshots and differences, run `npm run test:visual` and open the Playwright report with `npm exec -- playwright show-report visual-artifacts/report`. Failed comparisons retain expected, actual and diff images and traces under `visual-artifacts/results/`. CI uploads that directory as an artifact.

Only after reviewing an intentional homepage visual change, regenerate its baselines with `npm run test:visual:update` against the local build, inspect the PNG diff, and commit it. To capture production again, set `VISUAL_BASE_URL=https://event-driven.io` when running the update command. Do not update screenshots just to silence a regression.

To refresh only the two Firefox homepage references after reviewing production, run `VISUAL_BASE_URL=https://event-driven.io npm run test:visual:update -- navigation.spec.ts --browser firefox --grep 'homepage renders'`. Then rerun the same selection without the update flag or `VISUAL_BASE_URL` against the local build. This leaves Chromium references unchanged.

Adding articles or changing bio/article text requires no reference update. Current-source checks verify published content; component comparisons use controlled props. For an intentional component styling change, inspect `npm run test:components:review` and use `npm run test:components:update -- --grep 'en editorial components at 1440px'` only after explicit review. Rerun `npm run test:components:browser` without updating. CI and imports never enable updates. Commands and boundaries are in [testing-guidance.md](../../../docs/testing-guidance.md).

Playwright Test manages browser/context cleanup and local server startup. Its native screenshot assertion uses the existing PNG paths, requires identical dimensions, and preserves the pixel colour threshold of 0.2 and maximum differing-pixel ratio of 0.03. Normal runs use `updateSnapshots: none`, including missing baselines. Focus tests with `--grep` rather than Vitest’s `-t`.
